note: Coverage exemptions for the Channel 0.2 verification gates. `build/verify-channel-0.2-coverage.ps1` runs each covered gate under a line trace and requires every conditional in it to be evaluated by a passing run; a gate marked `measureOperands` is additionally run from an instrumented copy that records each operand of every `-and`/`-or` expression, and every operand whose expression was evaluated must have been evaluated too. An entry in `exemptions` declares one construct a passing run correctly cannot reach, and an entry in `operandExemptions` declares one operand short-circuiting correctly never reaches, each with the reason. Three classes are exempt structurally rather than by entry, in the gate itself: anything inside a `catch`, the `foreach ($failure in $failures)` loop each gate prints its findings with, and an operand whose whole expression was never evaluated -- that last one is the condition measure's subject, and reporting it here would report the facts gate's `-Apply` path a second time under another name. Those are expressed as a walk to the root, as the collection the loop walks, and as the expression's own evaluation, not as lists of the ones that exist today, because AN2 was a list that held eight of nine. The guard harness and the coverage gate are deliberately absent: AT4 measured both once and AT7 records why neither is measured on every commit, which is that covering either means running it and both are shaped so that running them is what costs.

authority.note: An exemption is a claim that a construct or operand cannot be reached by a passing run. It is not a way to quiet the measure: an entry whose construct is reached fails, and an entry whose construct no longer occurs fails as stale, on the same rule the probe corpus applies to a rotted anchor. A check that is unreachable because no input exercises it is a missing input and belongs in the vector corpus, not here -- which is AR1, and is why this file has no entry for the two property clauses that had no input, nor for the four AT1-AT3 operands the operand measure found the same way.

exemptions.reason: AK3's `N capabilities owe` claim. Every capability cell in the per-capability property audit is filled against an executable evaluator, so no capability owes a required-green set and no artifact makes the claim. The guard is dormant because the residual work it counts is finished, which is not the same as expired: it fires again the moment the claim reappears. The AQ pass read this one and reached the same conclusion.
The body of the dormant AK3 claim loop above. Unreachable for the same reason and for exactly as long.

operandExemptions.reason: The closed-vocabulary check on the closure-cycle state. The cycle is on hold, so the first operand is false on every clean run and short-circuiting never reaches this one. It is reached by the probe that declares a state outside the vocabulary, which is the input this operand exists for; it is exempt from the clean-run measure rather than unexercised.

The same closed-vocabulary shape on the operand-enumeration verdict column. Every row in the clean package records `sufficient`, so the first operand is false on every row and this one is never reached. AT5 added the probe that declares a verdict outside the vocabulary; as with the hold state, the operand is exempt from the clean-run measure and not from the corpus.

gates.argumentsWhy: The properties gate evaluates generated conforming vectors on every run, and tracing a hundred of them costs several times this whole measure. Fifteen is the smallest count that still satisfies the generator's own required-shape assertions at the declared seed -- a faulting session, an `establishing` route, a drained close, a session with no interaction, a vector with more than one session, and a wave that fills the bound -- so every construct in the generated block is reached without paying for a population this file is not the one measuring. A smaller count fails those assertions rather than silently narrowing what is traced. AZ3's dropped-field sweep is bounded separately for the same reason and by a much smaller number: it evaluates `C4-P2` eighteen further times per vector it covers, and under a line trace that took this measure from about ninety seconds to over ten minutes. Four is enough because every construct the sweep adds is reached by whether a vector carries one session or several, and at the declared seed the first four carry three, one, two and one -- so both branches of the scope test, all three outcome classes and all eighteen droppings are traced. A smaller count loses the single-session vector and fails the sweep's own coverage rather than silently narrowing what is traced.

exemptions.reason: Inside the branch that reports a property whose verdict is not the declared one. A passing run has no such property, so the message this line decorates is never built.
The same, for an operand mutation whose verdict is not the declared one.

AU2's report loop. A property reads a field through `Read-Required`, which records the absence rather than returning a verdict, and this loop raises each recorded absence against the vector. Every declared input publishes every field its properties read, so a passing run records none and the loop walks an empty collection -- it fires the moment a vector stops publishing one, which is what the AU2-a probe pins.

AU1's same-line refusal. Every obligation in this file is constructed on its own line, so the grouping selects nothing and the loop walks an empty collection. It fires the moment two verdicts share a line, which is what the AU1-b probe pins.

The cap on reported generated findings, inside the branch that records a field the generator does not publish. A passing run publishes every field its properties read, so nothing is recorded and the cap is never consulted.
The loop that turns recorded generated findings into failures. Empty on a passing run, for the same reason.

AZ1's report loop. An evaluator returns `Errors` beside its verdict to say it could not be evaluated over a record -- a reference carrying no operand, or one resolving to no declared step -- and this raises each one against the generated vector. A passing run generates records every property can read, so the collection is empty and the loop walks nothing. It fires the moment a generated reference stops resolving, which is what the AZ1-a probe pins, and which this block silently discarded until this pass.

Inside the branch that reports a dropped frame-reference field whose verdict is not the one the sweep declares for it. A passing run has no such dropping, so the message this line decorates is never built. The AZ3-a probe pins the branch.

operandExemptions.reason: The second of the two artifacts a named mutation may be stated in. Every declared mutation is named by the completeness review's per-capability audit, so the first operand is false for all of them and the contract is never consulted. The operand is a deliberate second source rather than a missing input: the contract names C4's two scenarios, and a mutation moved out of the audit into the contract alone must not become a failure. It is reached only by an input that has one and not the other, which no conforming package has.

The cap on reported findings, behind the test for a property red on a generated conforming vector. That first operand is false on every generated vector a passing run produces, so short-circuiting reaches the cap in no input. It is reached the moment the instrument finds something, which is when the cap matters.

The cap on reported findings, behind the test for a dropped field whose red arrives through a conjunct other than the one the sweep names it against. Every declared red fires through its named conjunct on a passing run, so the second operand is false throughout and short-circuiting reaches the cap in no input. The AZ3-b probe pins it by swapping a declared conjunct.
